newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Motor racing-Australia Grand Prix posts small loss.
newsitem.headline: Motor racing-Australia Grand Prix posts small loss.

text.p: The Victorian state government said on Tuesday the 1997 Australian Formula One Grand Prix held in Melbourne in March posted a A$2.7 million loss after a transport strike reduced ticket sales.
The Australian Grand Prix Corp, which runs the event, said the race attracted 289,000 spectators compared with more than 400,000 people the previous year.

"We are not suggesting the transport strike was the sole factor affecting ticket sales, but it was certainly a significant one which confused spectators and deterred others from coming," said Louise Asher, Victoria's Minister for Small Business and Tourism.
Melbourne's public transport workers staged a 48 hour strike over the time of the Grand Prix, in pursuit of a wage claim and better working conditions.

Asher said the government estimated the Grand Prix made a net gain of A$4 million after tax receipts of A$7 million were taken into account. This compared to a net gain of A$6.9 million for the 1996 event.
